Bitcoin has been retracing after the small range break, and I see it more like a retest, with a new lower low potentially following. Price is building liquidity below for the purge, so keep an eye on it and wait before building a fresh altcoin position.
---
The two largest upcoming options expiries, on November 27 and December 25, hold $5.7B and $12.5B in open interest. Their max pain levels, the price at which the largest share of open options expires worthless, sit at $80K and $76K, on either side of spot, so the options market adds no clear pull in either direction.

Across all expiries, traders hold about $18B in calls against $13B in puts. The largest December call positions sit at $80K, $90K, $100K and $120K, while the largest puts sit at $60K and below, as protection against a deep fall. This points to positioning for upside into year-end. Note that open interest does not show who bought and who sold: part of the call open interest is likely sold by holders to earn a premium, so not every call is a bet on higher prices.

📊    BTC On-Chain Update 

The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit, as BTC remains above its realized price — the average cost basis of all coins in circulation.

However, the margin is getting very thin, with  MVRV hovering just above 1 .

  ⚠️   A drop below this level would put the average holder into unrealized losses for the first time since early 2023.

The market is approaching a critical zone, and the next move will be important.

Bitcoin broke below the $60,000 level and faced heavy selling afterwards. The price dropped to $55,000 but is now experiencing a quick bounce from that point. The key level to watch is $60,000; a break above this level would signal a reversal of the downtrend.
